deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the surrounding pages. K is the 2-dimensional cell complex cut out by a finite family I of pseudo-lines; Grothendieck is axiomatizing it purely combinatorially. Each vertex s has a set I_s of pseudo-lines through it, with ν_s = |I_s|. The vector-arrow sets denote the corresponding sets of oriented pseudo-lines, which form ±1-double covers; →I_s has 2ν_s elements. On the previous page, each oriented line Δ through s gives a permutation u_{s,Δ} of →I_s. This is the rotation of oriented lines around s.

- (A2) requires u_{s,Δ} to be a single cycle whose ν_s-th power is the antipodal involution (reversing orientation).
- (30) states u_{s,-Δ} = u_{s,Δ}^{-1}. He sets →Z_{s,Δ} = {u, u^{-1}}.
- (A3) requires this pair to be independent of Δ. The common pair →Z_s is then a two-element set: the two local orientations ('senses of rotation') of the plane at s, with ±1 acting by swapping them.

This page.

(31) He builds a surjective, ±1-equivariant map from the oriented pseudo-lines not through s to →Z_s. Geometrically, RP^2 minus a line Δ is an open disk. An orientation of Δ, viewed as the boundary orientation, orients that disk and hence orients the plane locally at s. Reversing Δ reverses the local orientation.

Next, for an edge a of K joining s to s', he wants a transport map φ_a: →Z_s → →Z_{s'}, i.e. the parallel transport of local orientation along a. Let J be the oriented lines through neither s nor s'. J maps both to →Z_s and to →Z_{s'}. The axiom (A4) (transcribed as A9) demands that the two resulting quotients of J coincide: two oriented lines avoiding s and s' that induce the same orientation at s also induce the same orientation at s'.

Since both target sets have two elements and the maps are equivariant, φ_a is then a well-defined bijection, provided J is nonempty. The edges thus carry a combinatorial ℤ/2 local system on K, which is the orientation sheaf of the projective plane (nontrivial monodromy around a pseudo-line). The next page handles the degenerate case where J is empty or everything is concurrent: there he transports through an auxiliary triangle Θ, D, D'.
errors: Well-definedness of φ_a needs J ≠ ∅. Grothendieck notices this himself on the next page (the case where every line meets s or s', e.g. a concurrent family), so it is a gap acknowledged rather than an error.
Surjectivity of (31) onto the two-element set is automatic once one oriented line avoids s; it fails if every pseudo-line passes through s. That is the same degenerate case.
For genuine arrangements (A4) holds: no line other than the supporting line crosses the interior of an edge, so s and s' lie in the same component of RP^2 minus Δ. The axiom is consistent.

ideas.what: Local orientation at a vertex as the pair of opposite cyclic orders of the oriented lines through it
ideas.modern_name: local rotation / local sequences in pseudoline arrangements; rank-3 oriented matroid at a cocircuit

ideas.what: An oriented pseudo-line avoiding s induces an orientation of the plane at s, giving an equivariant surjection onto Z_s
ideas.modern_name: sign vectors / covectors of a rank-3 oriented matroid (side of a point relative to an oriented pseudoline)

ideas.what: Transport of local orientation along edges, with a compatibility axiom ensuring a ℤ/2 local system (the orientation cover of RP^2) on the combinatorial complex
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial orientation double cover / orientation local system of a cell complex

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axiomatization of pseudoline arrangements uses local cyclic data at vertices plus an orientation-transport axiom, a 'local system' style presentation. It is an alternative to chirotope axioms, and its equivalence with rank-3 oriented matroids is not proved in the notes. This is mild historical interest only, since the oriented-matroid literature covers the mathematics.
missed.quote: on obtient deux quotients de J — on demande la condition que c'est le même
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a local-to-global (sheaf-like) axiomatization of rank-3 oriented matroids. It might be of interest for comparing with local characterizations of chirotopes, but is likely equivalent to known results.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but routine combinatorial axiomatics of pseudoline arrangements, essentially subsumed by oriented matroid theory. The only distinctive feature is the local-system viewpoint on orientation transport.
transcription_corrections: The axiom label is most likely '(A4)', continuing A1–A3 from the previous page, not '(A9)'.
Final lines read roughly: 'ne passant pas par les extrémités s, s' de l'arête a, qui induisent la même orientation en s, elles induisent aussi la même orientation en s''.
In (31) the source is →I \ →I_s (all oriented pseudo-lines minus those through s), and the target is →Z_s.

The crossed-out phrase reads roughly 'isomorphisme ... besoin d'abord de' followed by 'l'existence de suffisamment de pseudo-droites qui ne passent pas par s ni s'' ('enough pseudo-lines'), not 'd'une bijection'.
